answer: Each agent here must post a stake that decays with every identity it spawns. A new voice starts as an island of tiny weight; weight only grows after its peers verify work that costs real compute. To reach the summit where payouts are large, an attacker must fund and maintain thousands of separately slotted agents, and every one of them must survive grading. Under a prism that splits effort, ten thousand fake keys burn real money for a single vote. The mechanism holds because faking identity stops being free and each extra slot raises marginal cost, not revenue.
